name: Medellín
title: Holidays in Medellín
intro: The 'city of eternal spring', with cable cars over hillside neighbourhoods, street art, coffee country and a mild climate all year. Here's what Medellín is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: Medellín's hillside neighbourhoods climbing the green valley under a stormy sky
facts_note: You fill in a free Check-MIG form online shortly before you fly. Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: Medellín is pleasant all year, around 27°C by day and cooler at night, thanks to its altitude. December to March and June to August are the drier months. August brings the Flower Festival, with farmers carrying huge flower displays on their backs, and December has the famous Christmas lights. Other months have afternoon showers.

things.name: Metrocable
things.blurb: Ride the cable cars up over the hillside neighbourhoods for huge views, on a normal metro ticket.

things.name: Comuna 13
things.blurb: A once-dangerous district reborn with street art, music and outdoor escalators. Go with a local guide.

things.name: Plaza Botero
things.blurb: Plump bronze sculptures by Fernando Botero outside the Museo de Antioquia.

things.name: Guatapé
things.blurb: Climb 700 steps up El Peñol rock, then explore a brightly painted lakeside town, 2 hours away.

things.name: Coffee farm tour
things.blurb: See coffee grown and roasted on a farm in the hills.

things.name: Parque Arví
things.blurb: Forest trails and a market at the top of the cable car line.

things.name: Bandeja paisa
things.blurb: The local feast of beans, rice, pork, egg, plantain and arepa.

faqs.question: Is Medellín safe to visit?
faqs.answer: Medellín has changed enormously and the main tourist areas are generally fine in daytime, but take care: use registered taxis or ride apps, keep phones out of sight in the street and avoid quiet areas at night. Check your government's travel advice before you book.

faqs.question: How many days do you need in Medellín?
faqs.answer: Four or five days covers the city, Comuna 13 and Guatapé. Add Cartagena or the coffee region for a longer trip.

faqs.question: When is the best time to visit Medellín?
faqs.answer: Any time, as it's mild all year. December to March and June to August are drier, and August has the Flower Festival.

faqs.question: How do you get to Medellín?
faqs.answer: Fly into José María Córdova airport, which has direct flights from Madrid and several US cities, then take a taxi or bus down to the city in about 45 minutes.

faqs.question: Where should you stay in Medellín?
faqs.answer: El Poblado and Laureles are the most popular areas for visitors, with good restaurants and easy access to the metro.
